title: Lesson 6: Worship and the Glory of God
description: Worship is gladly reflecting back to God the radiance of His worth. Through Paul and Silas singing at midnight, this lesson explores what it means to worship God in spirit and truth, not only on Sunday but with your whole life.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned to bring your pain to God and to trust that He is with you in the valley. Sometimes the most surprising thing that rises out of a valley is a song. This lesson is about worship, and it begins in a prison at midnight.

blocks.title: Songs at Midnight
blocks.text:
In the city of Philippi, Paul and Silas set a slave girl free from a spirit that had been used to tell fortunes. Her owners saw their income disappear, so they dragged the two men before the city officials. A crowd joined the attack. Paul and Silas were stripped, beaten with rods, and thrown into the inner prison with their feet fastened in the stocks.

Bruised and bleeding in the dark, they did something no one expected. "About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them" (Acts 16:25).

Suddenly an earthquake shook the prison. The doors flew open and everyone's chains came loose. The jailer woke, saw the open doors, and drew his sword to kill himself, sure that his prisoners had escaped. Paul shouted, "Do not harm yourself, for we are all here." The jailer rushed in, trembling, and fell down before them. "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" They told him, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household."

That same night the jailer washed their wounds, and he and his family were baptized. He set food before them, and he "rejoiced along with his entire household that he had believed in God" (Acts 16:34).

The prisoners were listening. Of course they were. They had never seen anything like it: beaten men singing, people in chains praising. Paul and Silas did not worship because their circumstances were good. They worshiped because their God was good. Worship that only happens when things go well declares our comfort. Worship that rises from a dungeon at midnight declares God's worth, and the whole world is listening for it.
6.1 - What would it look like for you to worship God in a hard place, not because things are good but because He is?
What Worship Actually Is

Most people think of worship as a style of music, or the part of a church service where someone plays guitar. But that is like saying eating is what happens in a restaurant. It might happen there, but eating is so much larger than that.

John Piper puts it this way: worship is gladly reflecting back to God the radiance of His worth. God is the sun, and you are the mirror. Worship does not start with you. It starts with God's worth, shining on you, and it ends with that worth reflected back to Him with joy.
Jesus said this to a Samaritan woman at a well, who wanted to argue about which mountain was the right place to worship:

But the hour is coming, and is now here, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father is seeking such people to worship him. God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.

Jesus moved the question from a place to a person. Worship in spirit comes from a heart the Holy Spirit has made alive, not from the right mountain or the right ritual. Worship in truth sees God as He really is, and Jesus is the truth (John 14:6). In Him the Father is fully seen. Worship that is only emotional without truth becomes manipulation. Worship that is only doctrinal without heart becomes a lecture. God wants both.

And notice the most surprising line: the Father is seeking such people. He sought out a Samaritan woman with a broken past. He sought out a jailer in Philippi. He is seeking you. Worship is not you trying to get God's attention. It is your response to a God who came looking for you first.
6.2 - In your own words, what is worship?
See, Bow, Receive, Go

Isaiah caught a glimpse of God's worth once. In a vision he saw the Lord, high and lifted up, with the train of His robe filling the temple. Seraphim called out, "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory!" The doorposts shook. Isaiah fell apart: "Woe is me! For I am lost; for I am a man of unclean lips." Then a burning coal from the altar touched his lips, and his guilt was taken away. When God asked, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?" Isaiah answered, "Here I am! Send me."

That is the shape of true worship. You see God clearly, you feel your own need, you receive His grace, and you respond with your life. Notice the order: grace comes before the sending. Worship is not a feeling you work up. It is an encounter that changes what you do next.
6.3 - When have you seen God so clearly that it changed what you did next?
Worship Is a Posture, Not an Event
After eleven chapters on the grace of God in the gospel, Paul turns to how we live, and he starts with worship:
I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.

Notice where Paul begins: by the mercies of God. You do not offer your life to earn His mercy. You offer it because you have already received it. Jesus was the one true sacrifice, given once for all. Because He died for you, you can live for Him.

And Paul says worship is presenting your body, your whole self. Your commute. Your workday. Your kitchen table. Your parenting. The way you handle money, anger, time, and relationships. Worship is not a donation of one hour on Sunday. It is a life laid on the altar every hour of every day. When you ask, Is what I am about to do reflecting God's worth, or am I reaching for a counterfeit?, that is worship thinking.
6.4 - Looking at an ordinary week, what does your life say you value most?
Why You Need the Gathered Church
Paul and Silas did not sing alone. Personal worship is real, but God designed worship to be shared with His people gathered together.

And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.

When your faith runs low, other people's faith helps carry you. Their voices carry the song when you cannot find the words. When you stand in a room full of people who have tasted and seen that the Lord is good, it strengthens what you know but may be struggling to feel. You need the body, and the body needs you.
6.5 - What has the gathered church given you that you could not have gotten on your own?
This Week's Practice

Pick one ordinary task you do every day, like making coffee, commuting, or cooking dinner. During that task, turn your attention toward God. Speak to Him, listen to a Psalm read aloud, or name one thing about who He is. Not a performance. Not an obligation. Just a turning toward the One who sought you first.
Also this week, read Psalm 95 and Psalm 96 out loud. Notice the words they use for God's character, and let one of them become your song for the week.
Lesson 6 Review

Paul and Silas sang at midnight, because God was good when their night was not. Worship is gladly reflecting back to God the radiance of His worth. It is offered in spirit, from a heart the Holy Spirit has made alive, and in truth, seeing God as He is revealed in Jesus. Like Isaiah, you see God, receive His grace, and answer, "Here I am." And by the mercies of God, your whole life becomes your worship.
In the next lesson, you will see how worship reaches all the way into your wallet.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
This lesson draws on John Piper's teaching on worship and the glory of God.
